Run every scenario of a project version in new R sessions

Source: R/run_scenarios.R
run_scenarios.Rd

run_scenarios() runs <home>/<version>_run.R once for each simulation of each scenario, each time in a new R session. It then stacks the simulations of each scenario and checks the assertions of the project.

Usage

run_scenarios(version, scenario = NULL, home = ".")

Arguments

version

The version, for example "v01".

scenario

NULL for every scenario, or a character vector of the scenarios to run.

home

The project folder.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of every assertion, with the columns scenario, assertion, expected, observed and pass.

Details

run_scenarios() does these steps in this order:

  1. It reads CFG$scenarios in a new R session that sources <version>_functions/ with org::initialize_project(). The R session of the caller does not change. It stops when a scenario other than "real" has no function expect_<scenario>(). It checks every chosen scenario before it runs any of them.

  2. It makes a plnr::Plan with one analysis for each scenario and simulation. Each analysis runs the script with callr::rscript() and the arguments scenario=<name> sim=<k>, with home as the working directory. A run that fails stops run_scenarios() with the output of the run.

    Before each run, run_scenarios() deletes the results.qs2 of that simulation. Before simulation 1, it also deletes the results.qs2 and the check.csv in <version>_results/<scenario>/. A run that writes no results.qs2 stops run_scenarios(). A run that quits with status 0 after it writes results.qs2 succeeds, so end_if_fake_scenario() can end the run of a fake scenario. Files of the scenarios that it does not run stay as they are.

  3. For each scenario with more than 1 simulation, it stacks the files <version>_results/<scenario>/sim_<kkkk>/results.qs2 into <version>_results/<scenario>/results.qs2. It stops when the files are not exactly the simulations 1 to sims. estimates, exclusions and each data.frame in tables get a first column sim. Each keeps the class of its object in simulation 1, so a data.table stays a data.table. extra is an empty list. The manifest is that of simulation 1. In it, sim and n_rows_data are NA, sims is the number of simulations, and stacked is TRUE. For a fake scenario, it stops when a simulation has no valid manifest$fake_md5, or when the simulations do not have one value of it.

  4. For each scenario that has a function expect_<scenario>() in <version>_functions/, it calls that function on the results of the scenario in a new R session. expect_real() is optional. The function MUST return a data.frame with at least one row and the columns assertion, expected, observed and pass. run_scenarios() writes it to <version>_results/<scenario>/check.csv and prints it.

Each of these counts as one failed assertion, and run_scenarios() writes it to check.csv too:

  • expect_<scenario>() stops with an error. The assertion holds the error message.

  • expect_<scenario>() returns zero rows.

  • expect_<scenario>() returns something other than a data.frame with the four columns.

After every scenario is done, run_scenarios() stops when a value of pass is not TRUE. The error lists the failed assertions.

See also

Other project setup: end_if_fake_scenario(), initialize_project(), use_scenario()

Examples

# \donttest{
home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_run_scenarios_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(home, "data"))
utils::write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:4), file.path(home, "data", "d.csv"))
writeLines(
  c(
    "CFG <- list(",
    "  scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c('real', 'null'), sims = c(1, 2))",
    ")",
    "fake_null <- function(dir) {",
    "  utils::write.csv(data.frame(x = rnorm(4)), file.path(dir, 'd.csv'))",
    "}",
    "expect_null <- function(results) {",
    "  n <- length(unique(results$estimates$sim))",
    "  data.frame(assertion = 'two simulations', expected = 2,",
    "    observed = n, pass = n == 2)",
    "}"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)
writeLines(
  c(
    'p <- pbn::initialize_project("v01", home = ".", data_raw = "data")',
    "d <- utils::read.csv(file.path(p$data_raw, 'd.csv'))",
    "pbn::save_results(",
    "  exclusions = data.frame(step = character(0), n_before = numeric(0),",
    "    n_excluded = numeric(0), n_after = numeric(0)),",
    "  estimates = data.frame(term = 'mean_x', estimate = mean(d$x)),",
    "  tables = list()",
    ")"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_run.R")
)
pbn::run_scenarios("v01", home = home)
#> pbn: scenario real, simulation 1
#> pbn: scenario null, simulation 1
#> pbn: scenario null, simulation 2
#> Assertions of the scenario "null":
#>        assertion expected observed pass
#>  two simulations        2        2 TRUE
pbn::read_results("v01", scenario = "null", home = home)$estimates
#>   sim   term    estimate
#> 1   1 mean_x  0.07921043
#> 2   2 mean_x -0.06364893

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
# }
